coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Building 12 Plaza and Market Square
record.summary: The roughly 1.5-acre 'social centerpiece' of the Pier 70 open-space network (D4D Section 3.9): Market Square between Buildings 2 and 12 and Parcel D, the Building 12 entry plaza on 22nd Street, a Maryland Street platform for vendors and food trucks, and possibly the retained structural frame of Building 15. Building 12 itself reopened in 2022 and Maryland Street's paving is done, but the plaza is a Phase 1 park still tied to adjacent vertical development.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- derived from a real, street-polygonized city block (not a diagram pixel-trace), subtracting Building 2, Parcel D, and Building 12's own committed geometries. This is a deliberate departure from pure diagram-tracing: since Figure 6.4.2's own green fill didn't precisely reach the real (satellite-corrected) edges of Building 2 and Building 12, using the real block boundary instead better matches both the drawing's evident intent (this block reads as fully built-out, buildings plus plaza, no gaps) and the satellite ground truth. The block polygon's north edge stops slightly short of Parcel D's own north edge (~14m, since the not-yet-built '21st St (NEW)' isn't in real street data) -- unioned with D's own extent to avoid an artificial gap there. Area (~1.38 acres) is close to, but still a bit under, the D4D's cited ~1.5 acres for this named space -- the remaining gap most likely reflects the plaza's true extent continuing south past the mid-block passage (labeled '15' on the diagram) into the block south of Building 12, which is not part of this feature.
notes.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155); named per Figure 3.4.1 - Overview of Public Spaces (p.52), zone 5.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within Brookfield's largely unaddressed 28-acre site.
notes.regulatory_context: Part of the Pier 70 D4D's Open Space Network (Section 3.9), approximately 1.5 acres, wrapping the historic Building 12 (and Building 2) on their west and south sides between Louisiana St and Maryland St.

facts.value: 3.9 'Building 12 Plaza and Market Square', zone 5 of Figure 3.4.1

Market Square (flanked by rehabilitated buildings and new construction on three sides, four access ways, a compact tree grove), Building 12 Entry Plaza south of Building 12 on 22nd Street, Maryland Street Platform, and the Building 15 structural frame pending a structural feasibility study
A pedestrian opening on 21st Street between Building 2 and Parcel D; the existing passageway through Buildings 2 and 12; a Building 12 entrance from 22nd Street; a direct entry from Maryland Street
Open-air markets, community gatherings, small performances; Market Square extends Maryland Street with coordinated paving to accommodate vendors and food trucks
Within the Phase 1 area (Port's 2026 Exhibit A) and part of the three acres of Phase 1 parks

open_questions: No Port Commission schematic design approval or construction record for Market Square or the entry plaza was found; the interim events documented by the Port took place inside Building 12 and under Building 15, not on a finished plaza.

Whether the Building 15 structural frame is being retained (the D4D marks it 'pending structural feasibility study'): the Port's June 2025 deck shows Building 15 relocated over 22nd Street but does not say what will remain of it.

No openly licensed or public-record post-rehabilitation photo of Building 12 was found (checked Wikimedia Commons -- geosearch, category and title search all came up empty for anything dated 2022 or later). Perkins&Will's Building 12 wayfinding photography (by Bruce Damonte, via DNCO's case study) and Pier 70's own project photography are copyrighted, but their press/media contacts may grant editorial, non-commercial clearance on request -- worth revisiting if someone follows up with them.
